description: Achilles tendinopathy — moderate, still running but asking about this week's tempo session. Dean must prescribe eccentric calf work and give a clear decision rule for the tempo.

user.name: Sofia
user.injury_notes: Left achilles — mild-to-moderate tendinopathy. Stiff for first 10 min of each run, settles. Some soreness the morning after harder sessions. Managing for 6 weeks.

recent_conversation.content: Tempo held at 7:35/mi — essentially on target. Left achilles check: how did it feel during and after?
Felt okay during — maybe a 2/10 tightness in the warm-up. Some soreness this morning.

inbound_sms: Easy run today felt fine — the achilles was stiff for the first mile as usual but then it settled. I have a tempo on Wednesday. Should I do it or back off?

ground_truth.notes: Sofia is asking a direct decision question about Wednesday's tempo. This is NOT a hold situation — the achilles is managing at mild-to-moderate, warming up and settling. Core passing criteria (score 7+): (1) give a clear decision rule for the tempo — e.g., 'check morning stiffness Wednesday. If it's no worse than usual (≤2/10), do the tempo shortened to 3mi of work instead of 4. If stiffness is above 3/10, swap for an easy run and push tempo to Friday'; (2) prescribe eccentric heel drops — named specifically: 'eccentric heel drops off a step, straight knee 3×15 + bent knee 3×15, after each run'; (3) NOT set injury_hold. A response that just says 'be careful' or 'listen to your body' without a specific tempo decision rule scores below 5. A response that names calf stretches but not the eccentric protocol (lowering slowly off a step) scores below 6.
